note: Seeded design: 32 drones (one per column, world 32x32), each cycling North by 2, harvest+replant with an interleaved Tree/Grass companion pattern -- not growth-pipelined, each drone fully waits before moving on. Only needed target-gating (seed's while True never terminated) and a water-topup guard (same fix as sunflowers (multi) 001). Smoke-test projections were badly wrong (5-harvest sample: ~8h, 64-harvest sample: ~68min) vs the real ~24,415-harvest run finishing in ~6 minutes -- true steady-state throughput needed a much larger sample to reveal. 001 scored it: 06:07.889, Global Rank #111, all 20 internal repeats clean. Leader time not yet checked -- see queue.md. RAISE-WATER-THRESHOLD-BLOCKING-GROWTH (002, 2026-08-18): CLOSED, no code change, no live run. wood_single's exp-004 found real Tree growth at water~1 is 4,412 ticks (7.87x faster than an old unwatered measurement); since this design blocks fully on growth with no interleaving, raising its 0.5 water threshold looked like a free lever. Reconsidered against 001's own numbers first: 588 water warnings already occur at the current threshold (32 drones sharing one pool -- more demand risks worse contention), and real per-drone efficiency (~2,912 ticks/harvest-equivalent) is already comparable to wood_single's hard-won 2,682, just via parallelism instead of interleaving. Premise didn't survive contact with existing numbers -- closed without spending a real cycle. See experiments/wood/002/hypothesis.md and result.md. A genuine full redesign (pre-seed + interleaving) remains a real but large, unattempted lead -- cross-drone Tree-adjacency avoidance in a 32-drone grid is harder than wood_single's single-drone case.
